'''Salvador Imperatore Marcone''' (born 11 March 1950) is a [[Chilean people|Chilean]] former [[association football|football]] referee. He officiated the opening match at the [[1991 FIFA Women's World Cup]], as well as the semi-final between the [[United States women's national soccer team|United States]] and [[Germany women's national football team|Germany]]. He was later on call as a reserve official for the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=WORLD CUP '94: 5 DAYS AND COUNTING : The Weight of the World : Greater Stakes, Stricter Emphasis on Rules Interpretation Have Placed a Heavier Burden on Cup Referees Than Ever Before|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1994-06-12-sp-3299-story.html|work=[[The Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=21 April 2013|date=12 June 1994|first=Grahame L.|last=Jones}}</ref>

Imperatore also refereed at the [[1993 FIFA U-17 World Championship]], the [[1995 Copa América]] and the [[1995 King Fahd Cup]]. A [[chemical engineer]] by trade, Imperatore suffered a [[stroke]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|title=Salvador Imperatore se encuentra estable dentro su gravedad|url=http://www.cooperativa.cl/noticias/deportes/futbol/arbitros-chilenos/salvador-imperatore-se-encuentra-estable-dentro-su-gravedad/2008-10-19/120809.html|publisher=[[Radio Cooperativa]]|language=Spanish|accessdate=21 April 2013|date=19 October 2008}}</ref>
